This appeal is filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the dismissal of the claim petition in MVC No.1181/2013 by the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Belagavi.

2. The brief facts of the case are that, On 10.07.2011 at 21:45 hours on Belagavi-Bagalkot road, in Godachi village, when the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA-22-B-5452 owned by respondent No.1 and insured by respondent No.2 parked the same in the middle of the road,
without any precautionary measures and putting on parking lights.

The husband of petitioner No.1,
father of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 and as well as the son of petitioner Nos.4 and 5 namely Sri.
Basavaraj @ Basappa rode his motorcycle bearing No.KA-48-J-7700 owned by respondent No.3 and insured by respondent No.4 which is colluded with the said parked offending truck to its hind side,
causing the death of the said Basavaraj.
The claimants being the legal heirs of the deceased made a claim of NC: 2024:KHC-D:11692 compensation and the same came to be rejected by the impugned judgment.

3. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for appellants/ claimants and learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 4.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the lorry truck bearing No.KA-22-B-5452 has been parked on the road during the night hours and there was no indication of parking by switching on the parking lights or any other indication and there were no other street lights and the deceased was driving his motorcycle has dashed to the said lorry parked on the road.
He contends that the said aspect can be seen in the spot mahazar/ Ex.P.5, photographs/ Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.11.
He contends that the whole negligence is on the part of the truck driver/ owner, who parked the truck on the road and therefore, the owner of the truck/ insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
5. He places reliance on the decision of the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Oriental NC: 2024:KHC-D:11692 Insurance Company Limited Bellary Vs. Bannemma and Others.

entities.text: Oriental NC: 2024:KHC-D:11692 Insurance Company Limited Bellary Vs. Bannemma and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He contends that the accident is of the year 2011, deceased was aged about 32 years survived by dependents.
Considering the said aspect, the appellants/ claimants are entitled for compensation.

6. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that even though the lorry is parked, the deceased ought to have been careful in driving his motorcycle and there was a space available to pass through and there was negligence on the part of the deceased who was riding the motorcycle.
He submits that the evidence on record is not sufficient to hold that the owner of the truck is negligent and he is only liable to pay the compensation.
He contends that at the most there is a contributory negligence on the part of the respondent No.1/ owner of the truck.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11692 8. Having heard the learned counsel, the Court has perused the material placed on record and the Court has gone through the impugned judgment and the Trial Court Records.
9.
Ex.P.5 is the spot mahazar, wherein it is mentioned that the spot of accident is having 30 feet width and having 3 feet kachha road.
Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.11 are the photographs of the scene of occurrence where a parked lorry, the motorcycle and the dead body of the deceased are seen.
On seeing the said photographs it is clear that the major portion of the lorry has been parked on the road.

So the incident has occurred in the night at 11:40 pm, the width of the road is 30 feet, having parked the lorry, it was incumbent on the owner/ driver to display the parking lights, hazard lights which is mandatory under the rules.
He had not followed the provisions and had left the vehicle in the middle of the road.
There is no evidence to show that there was sufficient light to see the vehicle.

The motorcycle rider was proceeding in the same lane in which the vehicle was parked NC:
2024:KHC-D:11692 in the night time.

Considering the similar case, the co- ordinate Bench of this Court has observed thus:
16.

Therefore, if we hold that the grounds of appeal are the test to decide whether the cross- objection is to be allowed or not, we will be re- writing the provision of Order XLI, Rule 22 of C.P.C.,
and as Rule 22 does not import any restriction on the right of the cross-objector, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company under the provision of Section 173 of the Act questioning the award on any ground would permit filing of cross-objections.

Therefore, by referring to Section 149 of the Act, we cannot opine that the Insurance Company's right of appeal being limited, the claimant cannot seek enhancement through cross-objections, in such appeal.

Having impleaded itself to question the claim on all grounds as a party to the proceedings the Insurance Company enlarges its right of defence which permits it to contest on all grounds available to the owner.
It stands at par with any other party in the proceeding and has a right to question the award on all grounds available.

In this view, the judgment cited by the Learned Counsel would not be applicable and in view of the decision of the larger Bench of the Apex Court and conspectus of provisions of Sections 149, 170 and 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the right of the cross-objector to seek enhancement cannot be curtailed.
With this observation, I over-rule the objection raised by Sri G.N. Raichur that the claimant's cross-objection is not maintainable.
Apart from technical objections raised, impugned award is assailed on the ground Tribunal has unjustifiably fastened act of negligence on the lorry driver, instead of rider of motorcycle.
I have re- apprised the evidence.
The victims were riders of a motorcycle, and the unfortunate incident has Smt. Shaila W/O. Basavaraj Koppad vs Shri. Mallari Devappa Kurade

The situs is highway; width of the road is 30.
The right road margin measured from the position of the lorry was 16 and the lorry had occupied the remaining 14.
It is also not in dispute the driver of the lorry was its custodian.
Having parked it, it was incumbent on him to have displayed parking light or hazard light which is mandatory under the rules.
He did not adhere to these provisions and had left the vehicle abandoned without warning.
There is no evidence to show the area was sufficiently lit to see the stationary vehicle.
The motorcycle rider was proceeding in the same direction in which the vehicle was parked at night to night.
18. Thus, we have here two classes of vehicles, viz., a lorry-heavy vehicle and a motorcycle-two wheeler.
No doubt the statement of witnesses show the rider rammed into the stationery vehicle creating a serious impact after colliding and suffered injuries.
Had not the vehicle been there, the unfortunate victim would have been saved.
Thus taking into consideration the position of the lorry parked covering more than 14 leaving only 16 on the right side is undoubtedly an act of negligence.
The concept of contributory negligence is based on the doctrine of equal contribution, that means, the act of negligence could be measured by the act of omission and also that of commission.
In the instant case, what we have to examine is, whether the motorcycle riders could have expected the vehicle to be parked to avoid colliding with it?
Since the place where it was parked, no motorist could have expected it, the question of the rider applying sufficient caution does not arise.
The precaution which the Insurance Company expected the motorcycle riders to take was not possible as they could not have expected the vehicle parked.

But so far as the driver and insurer of the lorry is concerned, he ought to have been conscious of the fact that he was abandoning the vehicle on the road which had virtually covered half the width and it was possible that motorists will find it difficult to negotiate it if there is oncoming traffic.
Even otherwise, he should have been conscious of the fact that he was causing obstruction in free flow of traffic.
Balancing the two, the person who is responsible for indulging in the act of commission has to be held liable rather than the person who had indulged in omission.

The fact that the driver of the lorry who was the custodian of the vehicle had parked it without flashing warning sign or hazard light has to be taken as a act of negligence which attracts the provision of Section 279, I.P.C., even though the lorry was stationary.

The record of investigation which comprises FIR and final report (charge sheet) filed under Section 173, Cr. P.C., shows the Investigating Officer has mechanically raised the charge for the offence under the provisions of under Section 279 and 304, I.P.C., against the riders of the motorcycle only on the basis that the lorry in question was stationary.
It is evident he has presumed the driver of the lorry cannot be proceeded for negligence as he was not in the process of driving the vehicle.

He was not investigated whether parking of the lorry covering a substantial portion of the Smt. Shaila W/O. Basavaraj Koppad vs Shri. Mallari Devappa Kurade on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177492779/
5 road without taking proper precautions was an act of negligence or not.

sentences.text: Consequent to this improper investigation, one of the deceased riders was arraigned as accused, but as he died, the charge abated.

21. While dealing with claims for compensation by victims of such accidents/ though report is filed by the Investigating Officer will be relevant for consideration, yet the Tribunal is not precluded from deciding the question of negligence in an action under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
10.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that the truck was parked as it's axel was broken and the charge sheet has been filed against the deceased who was driving the motorcycle.

The co-ordinate Bench in the case referred supra, has considered the similar situation wherein the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the parked vehicle in para Nos.20 and 21 which are referred to supra.
Considering the said aspects, the claimants evidence proved that there was no negligence in driving of the motorcycle and culpable negligence is on the part of the driver/ owner of the parked lorry.
12. Coming to the quantification, the Tribunal has not quantified compensation.
The deceased was aged 32 years as on the date of accident and accident has occurred in the year 2011.
The deceased has left behind the dependents/ the claimants who are five in number.
Considering the chart prepared for the Lok-Adalat, the notional income for the year 2011 is to be taken at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Considering the age of the deceased, he is entitled for future prospectus at 40% that comes to Rs.2,400/-.
Therefore, the 1/4th of the said income has to be deducted, which comes to(Rs.8,400 - Rs.2,100 = Rs.6,300/- x 12 x 16) Rs.12,09,600/-.
As the claimants are five in numbers they are entitled for - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11692 consortium in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (40,000 x 5).
The claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards the loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and transportation of the dead body.
Therefore, the appellants/ claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,39,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition, till its realization.
The entire liability is on the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer.
